answer: The cheapest real defence: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because onyx only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, canyon is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any plume approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
